hero.headline: An AI software agency where every worker has its own brain.
hero.subheadline: 66 AI workers in 12 divisions, each with its own model and plugins. One command starts them on your own machine.

pillars.heading: What makes it more than a prompt library

items.title: It does the work
items.body: Workers edit files and run commands inside a sandbox. What comes back is something you can open and check.

items.title: The checks live in code
items.body: You can talk a model out of following a prompt. You can't talk it past a failing test. Work that fails a quality gate stays inside the agency until someone fixes it.

items.title: Each worker has its own model
items.body: The Slice / Markup Engineer reads screenshots, so it gets a model with vision. The Task Dispatcher hands out tasks all day, so it gets something cheap and fast.

howItWorks.heading: What happens after you send a message

steps.title: You write a brief
steps.body: Drop the job into the agency's Telegram group, the way you'd explain it to a colleague.

steps.title: The planner breaks it down
steps.body: The Planner / Decomposer in Nexus splits the brief into tasks and hands each one to the right division.

steps.title: Divisions pick it up
steps.body: Compass works out the scope, Atelier designs it, and Forge builds it, each worker on its own model.

steps.title: Dev and QA go back and forth
steps.body: Crucible tests what Forge builds. Anything that fails goes back to the developer, and the loop runs until the tests pass.

steps.title: The Gatekeeper checks it
steps.body: Lint, type checks, tests, and accessibility checks run as code. A model can't argue its way past them.

steps.title: You approve the result
steps.body: A summary lands in Telegram with buttons to approve it or ask for changes.

divisions.heading: Meet the 12 divisions
divisions.intro: Each division is named after a room in the agency's headquarters. Open a card to see who works there.
divisions.waveLegend: Workers ship in three waves: 29 in the first, 20 in the second, and the last 17 in the third.

brains.heading: What's inside a worker
brains.intro: Each worker is a manifest with five slots. Swap the model or the plugins whenever you like. AMORA only refuses the change when the new setup can't do the job.

anatomy.body: The LLM doing the thinking. You choose it per worker.
Tools the worker can call, such as web search or a design canvas.
What it remembers from one task to the next.
A schema for what the worker takes in and hands over, so the next worker knows what it's getting.
Checks the output has to pass before anyone else sees it.

demo.heading: Try giving a worker the wrong model
demo.sameFamily: Same model family as {model}, which the {worker} uses. A reviewer has to come from a different family.
demo.differentFamily: Different family from {model}, which the {worker} uses.

telegram.heading: You run it from Telegram
telegram.intro: Each division has its own topic in the group. Workers post their handoffs there, and when something needs your decision, it shows up with a button.

messages.author: You
messages.text: Can you add a pricing page to the marketing site? Three tiers, with a monthly/yearly toggle.

messages.author: Planner / Decomposer
messages.text: Splitting this into 4 tasks: tiers and copy to Compass, layout to Atelier, build to Forge, tests to Crucible.

messages.author: Product Manager
messages.text: Draft tiers: Starter, Team, Agency. Yearly gets two months free.

messages.author: UX Architect
messages.text: Wireframe's up. The toggle sits above the cards and the Team tier is highlighted.

messages.author: Logic Developer
messages.text: Page is built. The billing period lives in the URL, so a shared link opens on the same plan.

messages.author: Unit & Integration Tester
messages.text: 12 tests, 1 failing: yearly prices round down by a cent. Sending it back to Forge.

messages.author: Gatekeeper
messages.text: Lint, types, tests, and accessibility all passed.

messages.author: Status Reporter
messages.text: Pricing page is ready for review. Ship it?

install.heading: Install
install.intro: AMORA runs on your own machine through Docker. You'll need an API key from at least one model provider.
install.notice: [PLACEHOLDER] Final commands will follow the repository README.

security.heading: Your keys stay on your machine

items.title: Secrets are encrypted
items.body: API keys are stored encrypted on the machine running AMORA. They never go through Telegram.

items.title: Code runs in a sandbox
items.body: Workers execute code in an isolated sandbox instead of directly on your computer.

items.title: You pick the providers
items.body: You decide which provider and model each worker uses. None of it is routed through us.

finalCta.heading: Try it on a small project first
finalCta.body: AMORA is open source and still experimental. Bring your own model keys.
